title: The strict-local fibre of a pseudo-open immersion
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be a morphism of Noetherian schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Assume that $|f|$ is a homeomorphism onto its image and that the natural map of sheaves of rings $f^{-1}\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal O_Y$ (the adjoint of $f^\sharp$ for the inverse image [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image]) is an isomorphism. For any geometric point $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ [def-weil-geometric-point], put $\bar x=f\bar y$ and form strict localizations [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit] using the same algebraically closed field $\Omega$. The canonical map $Y_{(\bar y)}\to X_{(\bar x)}$ is an isomorphism, and the natural map $Y_{(\bar y)}\to Y\times_X X_{(\bar x)}$ is an isomorphism. Equivalently, the commutative square with top arrow $Y_{(\bar y)}\to Y$, bottom arrow $X_{(\bar x)}\to X$, and right arrow $f$ is Cartesian. All arrows are the canonical maps induced by $f$ and the pointed strict localizations.

source.place: XVII Definition 5.2.1 and proof of Proposition 5.2.2(a),(c): ordinary geometric strict-local-fibre assertion underlying the stated trivial t-exactness and the derived counit isomorphism.

proof.text: Write $j_Y:Y_{(\bar y)}\to Y$ and $j_X:X_{(\bar x)}\to X$. Let $y$ and $x=f(y)$ be the underlying points. Let $\varphi:f^{-1}\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal O_Y$ be the assumed isomorphism, the adjoint of $f^\sharp$, so $f_*\varphi\circ\eta=f^\sharp$ for the unit $\eta$ of [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image]. By [lem-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image-stalk] (commutative rings) there is a ring isomorphism $c:\mathcal O_{X,x}\xrightarrow{\sim}(f^{-1}\mathcal O_X)_y$ with $c(s_x)=(\eta_V(s))_y$ for $s\in\mathcal O_X(V)$, $V\ni x$. Put $\alpha=\varphi_y\circ c:\mathcal O_{X,x}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal O_{Y,y}$. Then $\alpha(s_x)=(\varphi_{f^{-1}V}\eta_V(s))_y=(f^\sharp_V(s))_y$, so $\alpha$ is the stalk map $f^\sharp_y$ of [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism], and it is an isomorphism. Since $\bar x=f\bar y$, the two maps from these local rings to $\Omega$ satisfy $\mathrm{ev}_y\alpha=\mathrm{ev}_x$. Thus $\alpha$ identifies the embedded residue fields, and their separable algebraic closures inside $\Omega$ are the same field $K$. This is an identification through the given maps to $\Omega$, not an arbitrary isomorphism of separable closures.

source.place: XVII Definition 5.2.1; passing to germs in its structure-sheaf isomorphism

proof.text: Put $A=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and $B=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$. Choose affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}D\ni x$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}E\ni y$ with $V\subseteq f^{-1}(U)$; by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization](c) the germ maps identify $D_{\mathfrak p_x}\cong A$ and $E_{\mathfrak p_y}\cong B$, so the local rings $L$ of the comparison below are $A$ and $B$ with their germ maps from $D$ and $E$. By [lem-exc-affine-strict-local-ring-comparison], the geometric strict-local rings $C_X$ and $C_Y$ identify with algebraic strict henselizations of $A$ and $B$ relative to $K$, compatibly with structural maps and geometric evaluation. In the pointed-algebra colimit definition [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization], an etale $B$-algebra $(E,\chi:E\to K)$ is an etale $A$-algebra by composing its structural map with $\alpha$; the inverse operation composes an $A$-algebra structure with $\alpha^{-1}$. They leave $E$, $\chi$ and every morphism unchanged, and are inverse on the entire diagrams. On small representative categories as in the strict-local construction, their colimits therefore give mutually inverse maps $\beta:C_X\to C_Y$ and $\gamma:C_Y\to C_X$: on every colimit leg the composites are the identity, so the universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] makes $\gamma\beta$ and $\beta\gamma$ identities. The map $\beta$ extends $\alpha$ and preserves evaluation in $K$; its inverse does likewise.

source.place: Tag 04HX, lemma-describe-etale-local-ring, and algebra.tex Tag 04GW, lemma-strict-henselization-different; reindexing along an isomorphism of local rings

proof.text: Let $e=\operatorname{Spec}\beta:Y_{(\bar y)}\to X_{(\bar x)}$. It is an isomorphism by Step 2. It satisfies $j_Xe=fj_Y$: take an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}D$ containing $x$ and an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}E$ containing $y$ in $f^{-1}(U)$. Both composites factor through the open $U$ (the first by the structural equation of the comparison, the second since $V\subseteq f^{-1}(U)$), and morphisms from the affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}C_Y$ to $U=\operatorname{Spec}D$ are determined by their ring maps $D\to C_Y$ [lem-a1-locally-ringed-space-affine-adjunction]. The affine comparisons in Step 2 express the two composites to $U$ by the ring maps $D\to A\to C_X\xrightarrow{\beta}C_Y$ and $D\to E\to B\to C_Y$. They agree because $\alpha=f^\sharp_y$ (Step 1) makes $D\to A\xrightarrow{\alpha}B$ equal to $D\to E\to B$ (germs of $f^\sharp$, with $D\to E$ the ring map of $f|_V:V\to U$ and the identifications of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization]), and $\beta$ extends $\alpha$. The residue map of $\beta$ is the identity on the common $K$ by evaluation compatibility in Step 2. The uniqueness in clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality] now identifies $\beta$ with the canonical local ring map induced by $f$. In particular $e$ is the canonical strict-localization map in the statement, not merely some isomorphism between the two schemes.

source.place: Tag 03PS, definition-etale-local-rings, following functoriality paragraph; Tag 04HX, lemma-describe-etale-local-ring; algebra.tex Tag 04GU, lemma-strictly-henselian-functorial

proof.text: The morphism $f$ is a monomorphism directly from the hypotheses. If $a,b:T\to Y$ satisfy $fa=fb$, injectivity of $|f|$ gives the same underlying map $a=b$ on points. On that common inverse-image sheaf, the maps to $\mathcal O_T$ for the two composites are $a^\sharp\circ a^{-1}(f^\sharp)$ and $b^\sharp\circ b^{-1}(f^\sharp)$ in the inverse-image form of the composition rule in [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism], obtained through the adjunction $a^{-1}\dashv a_*$ of [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image]. The last factors coincide and are isomorphisms; cancel them to get $a^\sharp=b^\sharp$, hence equality of scheme morphisms. Now take any $a:T\to Y$ and $b:T\to X_{(\bar x)}$ with $fa=j_Xb$. Set $c=e^{-1}b$. Step 3 gives $f j_Yc=j_Xec=j_Xb=fa$; cancellation of $f$ gives $j_Yc=a$. Also $ec=b$, and the last equation determines $c$ uniquely. This is exactly the universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] for the displayed square. It follows that its canonical comparison $Y_{(\bar y)}\to Y\times_X X_{(\bar x)}$ is an isomorphism respecting both projections.
